pages.text: One morning, two children found two pumpkins in the garden.
One pumpkin was very big. The other was small.
The children looked carefully. Which pumpkin takes more space?
The bigger pumpkin takes more space. The smaller pumpkin takes less.
Later, they saw two trees. One was tall. One was short.
The taller tree reached higher into the sky.
Then they found two rocks. One felt heavy. One felt light.
The bigger rock was heavier. The smaller rock was lighter.
They learned something important: bigger and smaller depend on what we compare.
From that day on, they noticed size everywhere — in shoes, cups, and even clouds!
